title: Addressing Practical Issues in Atomic Force Microscopy-Based Micro-Indentation on Human Articular Cartilage Explants
protocol: Place cartilage samples in a container filled with DMEM supplemented with 5% (v/v) penicillin-streptomycin immediately after resection.
Ensure that cartilage samples are completely submerged in the medium and process within 24 hours of surgical resection.
Cut the cartilage away from the bone using a scalpel.
Generate cartilage discs of 4 mm in diameter using a biopsy punch.
Resect areas of the condyle where the cartilage layer thickness exceeds 1 mm.
Place previously generated 4 mm cartilage discs on a custom-made cutting device.
Fix and hold the cartilage discs stable using a spatula.
Position the samples so that the superficial zone of the articular cartilage does not face the blade.
Cut the cartilage discs with a razor blade to generate disc-shaped samples of 4 mm x 1 mm.
Collect each disc using a spatula.
Place the generated cartilage discs into 1.5 mL tubes containing 1 mL of DMEM supplemented with 5% penicillin-streptomycin.
Place approximately 15 discs in one tube.
Perform tissue cutting as quickly as possible to prevent sample drying.
Cover the cartilage disc with water-soluble embedding medium and place it on its edge on the cryotome knob (with the surface of the disc perpendicular to the surface of the knob).
Section the tissue sideways at a 60 μm thickness until the middle of the disc is reached using a standard cryotome.
Collect the slices when they reach a length of 4 mm.
Place one cartilage disc in each well of a 96-well plate.
Add 130 µL of cell permeable fluorescence dye at a dilution of 1:1,000 to each well.
Visually inspect the entire plate and ensure only one disc is placed in each well.
Incubate the plate for 30 min at 37 °C in a standard cell culture incubator.
Gently place cartilage disc sections on glass microscope slides using forceps.
Cover the cartilage sections with mounting medium containing nuclear DAPI counterstaining.
Place coverslips suitable for fluorescence microscopy over the mounted sections.
Seal edges of each coverslip with regular transparent nail polish and allow to dry for 3 min.
Place the 96-well plate on the plate holder of the fluorescence microscope.
Select the appropriate fluorescence filter for top-down imaging (Em 495 nm/Ex 515 nm) or side-view imaging (Em 358 nm/Ex 461 nm).
Use the 10x objective to inspect the whole circumference of the disc.
Determine visually the cellular pattern displayed in each cartilage disc.
Accept samples if undesired patterns are at the very periphery, up to 0.5 mm from the disc border, and do not exceed 10% of the total surface area.
Image acquisition of the entire cartilage discs.
Select the 10x objective of the microscope and position it underneath the preselected well containing an individual cartilage disc.
Focus on the disc to see the cellular pattern.
Select the Navigator Function to get an overview of the entire well.
Use the left mouse button and drag to navigate to a different stage position.
With the mouse wheel, zoom in and out.
Double-click on each area of interest sequentially to preview the well with the entire sample.
Select a square that encompasses the area of interest to be scanned.
Adjust the exposure/light intensity so that the cells can be clearly visualized from the background.
Examine the distribution of the signal in the histogram to evaluate if the exposure time is appropriate for a particular channel.
Use the automatic exposure mechanism included in the microscope's image software to visualize all the cells residing within the disc.
Select the software's Focus Map Point option.
Left-click in the center of each individual tile.
Select the option Focus Map.
Double-click on a tile in the list to display and bring it into proper focus.
Click Set Z to save the focal plan and proceed to the next tile.
Use the Linked Shading option incorporated in the software prior to the actual scan if necessary.
Press Start Scan after adjusting the focal plan for each individual tile.
Save, export, and correctly annotate the images.
Fix each preselected cartilage disc containing a cellular pattern in Petri dishes by means of biocompatible glue.
Add sufficient sample glue on the top, bottom, left, and right sides of the disc.
Cover the discs with 2.5 mL of Leibovitz's L-15 medium without L-glutamine gently to avoid detachment due to waves created by the medium.
Position the Petri dish in the AFM device's sample holder.
Turn on the Petri dish heater set to 37 °C.
Allow the tissue culture dish to reach the desired temperature.
Initialize the software setup as previously described.
Select a suitable glass block cantilever holder for liquid measurements and place it on the AFM head.
Secure the glass block in the AFM head using the locking mechanism.
Ensure that the glass block's reflective surface is straight and parallel to the AFM holder.
Place the cantilever on the surface of the glass block holder, resting it on the polished optical plane at the center.
Carefully place a silicone skirt on the base of the cantilever holder to prevent medium condensation.
Lower the cantilever in 100 µm steps using the stepper motor function until fully submerged in the medium.
Run a scanner approach with parameters described by Danalache et al.
Retract the cantilever by 100 µm once reaching the bottom of the Petri dish.
Calibrate the cantilever using the exact steps and run parameters described by Danalache et al.
Save and display the vertical deflection in newton (N) units after calibration.
Use the stepper motor function to retract the cantilever to 1,000 µm.
Use the CCD camera of the microscope to identify the AFM cantilever.
Position the AFM cantilever in a sample-free area of the Petri dish.
Start a scanner approach with the cantilever on a clean, sample-free area of the Petri dish.
Retract the cantilever 1.5 mm away from the bottom of the plate using the stepper motor control.
Switch to fluorescence view and visually identify the top of the disc.
Move the AFM sample holder exactly 2 mm toward the middle of the disc.
Consider this point as the center of the cartilage disc.
Run a scanner approach until the surface of the cartilage disc is reached.
Retract the cantilever by 100 µm once the surface is reached.
Focus on the cells in the desired measurement site.
Click the Run button to start force-distance curve measurements.
Acquire five force-distance curves at each measurement site.
Retract the cantilever by 500 µm after acquiring the curves.
Move the cantilever to the next measuring site.
Select a minimum of five different measurement sites on the cartilage disc surface.
Acquire a minimum of five force-distance curves at each selected site.
Inspect and save the generated force-distance curves for analysis.
Open the generated force-distance curves in data analysis software using the Open a Batch of Spectroscopy Curves option.
Select the Hertz fit model within the software.

Choose the Elasticity fit option to automatically process the selected curve, including baseline subtraction, contact point determination, tip-sample separation calculation, and automatic fitting with the Hertz model.
Adapt using a Poisson ratio of 0.5 and the appropriate cantilever tip radius.
Use the Hertz fit model when the cantilever has a spherical tip with a radius of 5 µm.
Fit the force-distance curve until the maximum applied force is reached (setpoint).
Check visually the force-distance curve fit for correctness.
Open each generated force-distance curve in the data analysis software.
Select the Hertz fit Model as the analysis process.
Apply the Subtract Baseline Offset option to zero the vertical deflection axis (y-axis).
Select the Offset + Tilt function.
Use the Find Contact Point function to automatically identify the contact point, setting it at an x-coordinate of zero.
Subtract the distance accounting solely for cantilever deflection from the raw piezo height during the indentation using the Vertical Tip Position function.
Select the Elasticity Fit option to display the processed force-distance curve.
Select the area of the graph so that it lines up with the most negative value on the Vertical Tip Position Axis (x-axis).
Read and document the indentation from the X Min box in the parameter tab.
Save and document the results.
Open the statistical software.
Select New Dataset from the drop-down menu.

Define the numerical variables for each cellular pattern category: single strings = SS, double strings = DS, small clusters = SC, big clusters = BC, diffuse and the Young's moduli in Variable View tab.
Enter the measured Young's moduli data for each of the corresponding cellular pattern categories in Data View tab.
Analyze the data distribution by selecting Analyze from the menu bar, then Exploratory Data Analysis.
Select Young's Moduli as the dependent variable and Cellular Pattern as the factor list.
Conduct a statistical analysis by choosing Dependent Samples in the nonparametric test section of the analyze menu bar tab.
Select Young's Moduli as Test Fields and Cellular Pattern as Groups under the fields tab.
Press Run.
Incorporate the nonparametric test's p-values into the box plot.
Save the results by clicking File in the menu bar and selecting Save.
